The jar's contents after k removals are exactly the last 10−k balls of the removal order. So "at some time the jar has more blue than red" is equivalent to "some suffix of the removal order has more blue than red". Reversing the order gives another uniformly random arrangement, so I can ask instead whether some prefix of a random arrangement has more blue than red.

There are C(10,2) = 45 equally likely arrangements of the 2 blue balls among the 10 positions.

A prefix has more blue than red in exactly these cases:

- **First ball is blue.** The prefix is 1 blue and 0 red. There are 9 such arrangements, one for each position of the other blue ball.
- **First ball is red.** Then only 2 blue balls are available, so blue exceeds red only when the prefix has 2 blue and at most 1 red. Since it starts with a red ball, that means the sequence begins R, B, B. The remaining 7 balls are all red, so there is 1 such arrangement.

The favorable count is 9 + 1 = 10, so the probability is 10/45 = 2/9.

Thus a = 2 and b = 9, and 100a + b = 200 + 9 = 209.

ANSWER: 209
